delete.summary: Purge a document by lineage: its bytes and everything derived from it
delete.description: Deletes the document's bytes, every artifact lineage derives from it (an index built with it included, and training sets and models built from those), their stored parts and index tables, and the question candidates drafted from it that weren't accepted; trained models that lose their artifact are withdrawn. Its row stays as a tombstone (`withdrawn`, reason `deleted`), since frozen corpus versions and run records name it. Owners only; it can't be undone. Purging a withdrawn document again clears what's left.

post.summary: Mine a training set from a dev eval run: positives, hard negatives, traps
post.description: 202 with the queued set. Positives are the chunks of the expected document versions that cover each item's evidence, from the whole index; hard negatives are what the chosen checkpoints ranked that covers no evidence, traps (avoid, must_not_return) first. Only the dev split may be mined: dev items that nearly duplicate a test query are dropped. An identical set reuses the records.

A training set as JSON Lines: sentence-transformers, cross-encoder or chat
get.description: sentence-transformers: anchor, positive, negatives (one row per positive). cross-encoder: query, passage, label (1 for positives, 0 for negatives). chat: the pinned grounded-qa-v2 prompt over gold and distractor passages, answered with the item's reference answer and its citations, or the refusal when the item has no evidence; items with evidence but no reference answer are left out. Every row names its item and split.

get.description: A `text/event-stream` of JSON `data` lines. `event: job`: `workspace_id`, `job_id`, `kind`, `status`, `attempts`, and `progress` or `error_code` when present. `event: run`: `workspace_id`, `run_id`, `status`, and `counts` (tasks by status, by stage, and entries by state) when present. `event: eval_run`: the same, with the eval run's ID as `run_id` and `counts` of shards by status and queries. `event: experiment` and `event: test_run`: the same, with the experiment's or the test run's ID as `run_id`. Comment lines keep the connection alive. Events are hints: read state from the API after reconnecting.
